scope: Renaming a safety tag through a single tag_set with safetyAcknowledged=true: scripts/qualify_safety_drive_tags.py --safety-tag-rename on a Debug build of 90d20b07, 32/32 steps (artifacts/sd/n3), and the same runner without the flag as regression guard, 21/21 steps (artifacts/sd/n2), each in one owned TIA V21 scratch with an added CPU 1511F-1 PN 6ES7 511-1FL03-0AB0/V4.1 (configureScratchSecurity, failsafeRuntimeAccess; owned scratch only) as IO controller of a SINAMICS G120C PN 6SL3210-1KE21-3AF1 (firmware 4.7.14) with PROFIsafe telegram 30, inserted by the native fixture helper. With the real safety tags SafeDrive_S_ZSW1 (%IW0) and SafeDrive_S_STW1 (%QW0) in place, eight preparations were refused and software_inspect showed every tag unchanged after each: the rename without safetyAcknowledged (SafetyBoundary), safetyAcknowledged false (InvalidRequest), a new LogicalAddress (SafetyBoundary), a new DataTypeName beside the new Name (SafetyBoundary), a name another tag has (ObjectExists), safetyAcknowledged on a standard tag, on tag_delete and beside items (InvalidRequest each). The acknowledged rename of SafeDrive_S_ZSW1 to SafeDrive_Status then prepared with safetyTagRename, safetyBefore and the warning in its preview, and applied with checkpoint, baseline compile, safety_tag_rename_verified, compile (0 introduced errors) and save. The tag read back as SafeDrive_Status at %IW0, Word, isSafety true; the old name was gone and every other tag was unchanged. The four offline signatures (collective, software, hardware, communication address) and the F-runtime group were identical in safetyBefore and safetyAfter. change_restore of the rename returned the checkpoint. The regression run repeats local.safety.tag-batch.20261111 unchanged: every batch touching a safety tag or the telegram's addresses is still refused.
limitations: No block of the safety program used the renamed tag: the scratch F-CPU holds only the generated, empty main safety block. What a rename does to the signatures of a safety program that uses the tag, and whether it then needs a new acceptance, is not observed.
One Word safety tag of a PROFIsafe telegram 30 on one owned F-CPU 1511F-1 PN; safety tags on F-I/O modules, tags in software units and tags in user tag-table groups are not exercised.
The safety offline program had no password, so the SafetyLoginRequired refusal is covered by the shared guard of the other safety kinds only, not by this run.
The PROFIsafe telegram was inserted by the qualification fixture, not by an MCP route. No safety acceptance, password or download; engineering evidence only, not machine safety acceptance.
